title: Human review points: flags, timed soft reviews and hard approval gates (M)
description:
Human review is not expressed as story states. Any automation or step can raise a review request on an item (story, proposal, reference or automation output). Approach (Ryan): explore by building it, using it and seeing how it works, so ship the smallest version first.

A review request has: a reason; what is asked; who can answer (editor or admin); and one of three modes:
- flag: informational, nothing waits;
- soft review: the process waits until a deadline, then continues without the human if nobody answers, and records "proceeded without review";
- hard gate: the process never continues without an explicit approve or reject.
Answers are approve, reject, or feedback text. Feedback is passed to the next step as input.

Smallest first version: the backend ReviewRequest model, the three modes, the run contract honouring them, and the answer API the Notification Center uses (the console UI is the Notification Center story, replacing a separate review inbox). Email to editors comes second; Slack is optional later.

Scope:
- Backend model and an audit trail on the item.
- Deadline handling: a scheduled check that resumes timed-out soft reviews.
- The run contract (PPY-433383) honours gates: a run waits on a soft review or hard gate and resumes with the answer or feedback.
- Notifications, starting with email to editors.
- Recipients: per-site configuration, per review mode and/or per automation, listing editor or admin users plus optional extra email recipients, defaulting to the site owner. Changeable without a code change (the hard-gate approver for Distinctive's ruling stories is not decided yet).
- The console UI for answering requests is the Notification Center story (PPY-1cd261); A provides the model, answer API, deadline and gate logic.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each mode behaves as defined: a flag never blocks; a soft review that times out continues and records "proceeded without review"; a hard gate blocks indefinitely until approve or reject.
- Feedback text reaches the next step as input.
- Only editors and admins can answer; every request and answer appears in the item's audit trail.
- Recipients resolve from site configuration per mode and per automation, default to the site owner, and can be changed without a code change.
- Answers can be submitted through the answer API used by the Notification Center.
- Gherkin specs (narrative, complete) required.

Depends on PPY-433383 and the automation records story (PPY-2e6e2b). Dependency of the Notification Center, story-state triggers, idea pipeline and similarity index stories.

Product direction (Ryan, 2026-10-23): the Notification Center is the CMS console home, the first thing an editor sees after sign-in. Interacting selectively with a stream of review and steering opportunities, and ignoring some of them and letting them run, is the primary editor experience on sites with private backends. If you only look, the system keeps doing what it is doing; if you steer, it incorporates that steering as it moves forward. Everything except hard gates is ignore-safe. See docs/notification-center.md.
